The later two add words not in the Russian to carry the relation. Tolstoy himself says вы and its dictionary equivalent vous differ in coldness. A documented instance of the compensation mechanism; the evidence on what readers recover is translators' and the author's, not readers'. | Active |
| [CASE-067](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-067.md) | The reception of Deborah Smith's The Vegetarian: the Booker judges' task, the Korean critics' task, and one critic's two verdicts | Deborah Smith's English version of Han Kang's 채식주의자 won the 2016 Man Booker International Prize, while Korean critics published lists of errors and charged it with embellishment. Each side's task is stated in print: the judges evaluate "the finished English-language work on their own terms", while assessment in Korea "does usually involve comparison". Charse Yun perceives what both sides perceive and gives two verdicts by changing task. Part of the split is access, not weight: some errors are invisible to readers without Korean. | Active |
| [CASE-068](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-068.md) | Risk messages passed down diffusion chains: the evaluative signal kept and amplified while the content decays (Moussaïd, Brighton and Gaissmaier; Jagiello and Hills) | In two serial-reproduction experiments on risk messages, each link's message was coded for content and, on a separate scheme, for the evaluative stance of its statements toward the hazard. Content got shorter, less accurate and more divergent; the evaluative signal survived and drifted negative, and re-exposure to the balanced source did not undo the drift. The transmitters' own risk perception, measured by questionnaire, predicts the direction of the change. Documented chain evidence for evaluative stance; none for footing. | Active |
| [CASE-069](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-069.md) | Labov's recorded sounding sessions: ritual insult turning personal, with the same exchange shape and a different act | Labov's team taped sounding among Harlem peer groups. Boot answers David's taunt with a remark "related to A-5 in exactly the way that one sound is related to another", yet both are taken as personal insults: denied, objected to, wept over. Labov's rule puts the difference in a further relation, the shared knowledge before an audience that the proposition is untrue. A documented, non-institutional case for [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) in which the act follows a relation among the parties, and for [CLAIM-138](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md), since the exchange relations alone match and the acts still differ. | Active |
| [CASE-070](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-070.md) | Voita, Sennrich and Titov's BLEU-tied translation systems that differ on keeping ты or вы across sentences | Two English-to-Russian subtitle translation systems score the same BLEU (32.40 and 32.38, not significantly different). On a contrastive test built from held-out films, which asks whether a system keeps the T or V form of "you" consistent across sentences, one is at chance (50.0%) and the other is right in 81.6% of cases. A documented instance, on a pragmatic distinction, of two realizations equal under a standard probe family and different under an independently built one. An ML paper that neither record holds. | Active |
| [CASE-071](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-071.md) | Kovacs, Deutsch and Freitag's metric bias in MBR decoding: translations a metric selects, that the metric and its neighbours rate better and human raters do not | Minimum Bayes risk and quality-estimation decoding pick, from 128 sampled translations, the one a neural metric scores best. That metric and other neural metrics rate the picks significantly better than greedy decoding; human MQM raters find them no better, and for four system and language-pair combinations significantly worse. [CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md)'s result in text, by selection rather than training. The distinction lost is accuracy, not a pragmatic one; a stipulated English-to-Russian ты/вы variant states the design that would make it pragmatic. | Active |
| [CASE-072](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-072.md) | Hafez's "Shirazi Turk" in English: one ungendered beloved rendered as a maid, as God and as a boy | The opening of Hafez's ghazal 3 names a beloved, "that Shirazi Turk", whose sex and nature the Persian leaves open. English forces a choice at the first possessive. Jones (1771) and Bell (1897) make the beloved a maid, Clarke (1891) makes it God, and Davis (2012) makes it a boy, and Davis says in print that his choice is arbitrary. A documented instance of the half of a change of cover in which the rendering decides what the source left open. The disagreement on the source is among translators and scholars; no reader agreement has been measured. | Active |
| [CASE-073](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-073.md) | The Kia Provo: one concept-car name, a blank coinage to the motor press and taken as honouring the IRA in Northern Ireland | In March 2013 Kia showed a concept car at Geneva named the Provo, "from the word 'provoke'". The motor press found no meaning in the name; in Northern Ireland, where "Provo" names a member of the Provisional IRA, six MPs said it "has caused deep offence". Kia said it meant no offence, and withdrew the name for the UK and Ireland. One name, the speaker's intention fixed and declared, a new audience, and an unintended reading taken up and acted on: the accidental, verbal variant of [CASE-064](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-064.md), illustrating [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md). | Active |
| [CASE-074](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-074.md) | Twitch Plays Pokémon in democracy mode, with the running tally shown while the votes come in | The crowd of [CASE-075](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-075.md) in democracy mode. Each move is the button that collects the most votes in a short window, and the running tally is shown while the votes arrive, so the current majority can sway the votes still coming. The owner judges it a better demonstration of a population with drift-diffusion decision dynamics than anarchy mode. Showing the tally adds feedback, and feedback moves the dynamics toward winner-take-all. | Active |
| [CASE-075](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-075.md) | Twitch Plays Pokémon in anarchy mode: one avatar steered through the map by the running aggregate of a crowd's inputs | In February 2014 a stream let everyone in its chat play one copy of Pokémon Red at once, with every typed button press executed in turn. The owner offers its navigation as a working approximation of an agent made of a population whose decisions follow drift-diffusion dynamics. The crowd's direction reorganizes continuously and is not switched. The record holds no source for the case yet. | Active |
| [CASE-076](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-076.md) | Twin pattern-keepers: two systems keep the same pattern, one by its own responses and one through an external controller, and only removing the controller tells them apart | A10 §3.3's paired design, the case behind [QUESTION-086](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md). Matching behaviour and persistence, different organization. Removing the controller destroys one system's pattern and not the other's. A10 then made it harder: the internal regulator at one scale is supported by other processes at another, so which side of the boundary the controller sits on depends on where the boundary is drawn. | Active |
| [CASE-077](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-077.md) | The reciprocal pair: two processes that endorse only each other under recursive delegation, so that each one's authority returns to it through the other | A2 §5's counterexample to the ban on self-endorsement: "Suppose D1 endorses D2, and D2 endorses D1." Under g = (1 − η)b + ηEᵀg, each operator's authority comes partly from its own endorsement returned after two hops. It came back in A6 as authority that "may circulate". Used to show that a ban on self-endorsement does not make authority independent of one's own endorsements. | Active |
| [CASE-078](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-078.md) | Who keeps placing on r/place: the proposed survival analysis of the released placement logs, testing whether participants return while their art survives and whether unaffiliated placement cools | Proposed by the owner on 2026-10-13, not run. On the released 2017, 2022 and 2023 logs, model each participant's hazard of stopping, with the survival of the art they placed into as a time-varying covariate, and estimate the rate of placements that fit no artwork over the event. The main threat is reverse causality: persistent defenders keep their art alive. So the design leans on destruction the participant did not cause, such as the 2022 moderator wipes and large raids. It is the test named in [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md)'s defeater. | Active |
| [CASE-079](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-079.md) | r/place: a shared pixel canvas on which each Reddit user could place one pixel at a time under a cooldown, and communities coordinated off the canvas to build, defend and overwrite images | The owner proposed it at U8 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: "every user can modify a single pixel once, and different subreddits coordinated to present certain images or even warred amongst each other over regions of the canvas". Reddit ran it in 2017, 2022 and 2023, and released the 2022 placement log. A8 read it as the exchange's two canvases made visible: the pixels as the meaning canvas, the plans, templates and alliances off the canvas as the influence canvas. First time the thing turns up in the record. The event and the data are documented. The readings of them are proposals. | Active |
| [CASE-080](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-080.md) | The skeptic who delegates: a critic that cannot overturn an emerging consensus gives its authority to a process that can generate alternatives | A3 §6's worked example. Four processes: an integrator and a decision- maker push toward a decision, a skeptic disagrees, and a generator can translate neglected evidence into new hypotheses. The skeptic does not try to win. It endorses the generator, whose hypotheses change the decision landscape. Used to show delegation as a route to one's goals, and dissent made useful by a role. | Active |
| [CASE-081](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-081.md) | Self-maintenance learned for a designer's reward: a system that maintains itself because it was trained to, and later revises the policy and keeps maintaining itself without further instruction | A10 §6.1's boundary case, "a system that learns to maintain itself only because an external designer rewards that behavior", with its question whether the maintenance becomes endogenous "once the system can revise the policy and maintain the associated governance without continued external instruction". It is the case [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) is about, and the place where that objection could be answered. | Active |
| [CASE-082](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-082.md) | The sufficient posterior without its history: a Bayesian agent that keeps only its current posterior updates as well as one that keeps everything, and cannot say how it got there | A6's fourth case, which A6 called "probably the most important counterexample in the set". It grounds the redundancy half of [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md) and one of [CLAIM-299](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-299.md)'s separations. A6's reserve case, revising the model class, is where it stops holding, and [CASE-087](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-087.md) is that case. | Active |
| [CASE-083](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-083.md) | A pseudorandom generator's output against uniform strings: almost disjoint in total variation, indistinguishable to every efficient test if the generator is secure | A15 §2's witness, which A15 recommended filing "with its cryptographic assumption explicitly stated". It grounds [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) and, by the record's own reduction, [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md). Checked against Goldreich (note of 2026-10-15): the definitions match, and the separation needs the generator only for samplability. | Active |
| [CASE-084](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-084.md) | The perfectly accountable false theory: a community whose record traces every commitment and whose vocabulary leaves out the right explanation | A6's third case. Accountability without correctness, one of [CLAIM-299](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-299.md)'s three separations, and A6's "direct companion to [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) and [CLAIM-190](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-190.md)". | Active |
| [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md) | The medication in the ambulance: a drug the EMT knew was stocked could not be found during a resuscitation, the paramedic changed the request, and afterwards said "If I can't find it, it isn't there" | The owner's own experience as an EMT-B on an ALS unit, told at U16. It illustrates [CLAIM-296](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md) and is the source of [TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md). Stipulated, not documented: the event is real, and the only source is the owner's retrospective account, which a reader cannot check. | Active |
| [CASE-086](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-086.md) | The retracted finding and its descendants: an experiment fails to replicate years after three conclusions were built on it | A7's sixth case, filed at the owner's U7 as an illustration and not a test ("one or two of those might be handy to keep on hand too"). Tracing descendants of a defeated premise, which [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) says a record of dependencies supports. | Active |
| [CASE-087](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-087.md) | The discredited instrument and the second population: two pairs of readings with the same mean that the mean cannot tell apart once one instrument is discredited or a mixture is considered | A10 §2's paired construction, which A10 recommended filing ("That single paired construction makes the dependence of sufficiency on the task and model very easy to see"). It grounds the relativity half of [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md). | Active |
| [CASE-088](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-088.md) | The repeated objection and the argument nobody reuses: filing pays for itself after a few recurrences in one case, and never in the other | A11's CASE B and CASE A, the arithmetic of [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md). | Active |
| [CASE-089](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-089.md) | The compensating evidence problem: two records with the same support graph in which discounting one support leaves odds of 20:1 or of 1.1:1 | A6's second case. It grounds [CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md): the same edges E₁ → H ← E₂, different Bayes factors for E₂, different revisions when E₁ fails. | Active |
| [CASE-090](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-090.md) | The rehabilitated hypothesis: an objection that displaced a hypothesis turns out to rest on a faulty measurement, and the hypothesis can be reopened because its defeat was recorded | A7's seventh case, the companion to [CASE-086](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-086.md) and filed with it. Reopening an alternative when its defeater is defeated. A12's "defeat of a defeater" is the same case and is held here, as A12 itself proposed. | Active |
| [CASE-091](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-091.md) | A memory ablation for revision: synthetic inquiries with known ground truth, run under six kinds of persistent memory, with information and token budget controlled separately | A6's fifth case, refined from A3, A4 §4 and A5. The design [QUESTION-108](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-108.md) asks for. Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-092](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-092.md) | A minimal coupled meaning–influence model: two hypotheses, two retrieval specialists, a fixed balanced corpus, queries set by the dominant interpretation and endorsement updated from apparent retrieval success | A22 §7 and A23 §XI, a simulation not yet built. It is how [QUESTION-100](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-100.md) would be answered and [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md) tested, and what [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) asks of the operator framework: a prediction a simpler model does not make. | Active |
| [CASE-093](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-093.md) | Same marginal, different updates: two joint distributions over a hypothesis and a condition that agree on the hypothesis and disagree on how to revise it | A6's first case, made exact at A8. It grounds [CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md). | Active |
| [CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md) | The LEGO bin: a brick owned in one copy and buried among hundreds of similar ones may as well not be owned, a black brick among white ones needs no bin of its own, and every brick can be found by going through the whole collection | The owner's own parable, told on 2026-07-02 and kept verbatim in Mathematics of Meaning, where the owner paired it with the EMT case this record holds as [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md). It is the second time that case's pattern has turned up, so it gets a code. It adds three things the EMT case lacks: similarity to binmates as the cause of the failure, copy count and frequency of use as what decides whether a bin is worth making, and exhaustive search as the reason presence is never in doubt. Stipulated: the collection is real, and its facts are taken on the owner's account. | Active |
| [CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md) | Two builders sorting one collection: the brick that one bins as red and two-wide and the other as a curved connector has a bin that respects both, and what the builders cannot share is an arrangement, not a description | The example the owner's LEGO monograph (Mathematics of Meaning, "The Lego Parable") uses for contextuality, rebuilt. As descriptions the two sortings always share a joint refinement, the product bin, as [MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md) shows, so they illustrate the non-contextual case of [CLAIM-037](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-037.md) and [CLAIM-131](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-131.md). As arrangements, with a fixed number of bins, they compete, and which wins depends on the queries made and on what stands out within a bin. Fictional: the builders and the collection are invented. | Active |
| [CASE-096](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-096.md) | The smoothie: milk makes it better for a while and then worse, unless there is more of everything else | The owner's line, the prompt the smoothie note in Part III of the LEGO monograph answers: "if I put milk in my smoothie, it gets More Good for a while until it gets Less Good, unless there's more of all the other stuff." The note's first model reads it right: a preference over the milk fraction, single-peaked, kept by scaling everything together. Its second reading, in signal detection terms, has the direction wrong ([CLAIM-309](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md)). Stipulated: the preference is the owner's, taken on the owner's word. | Active |
| [CASE-097](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-097.md) | The monograph's castle topic, persistent across refinement by construction, persists as no eigenmode: in its rank-2 and rank-3 co-occurrence matrices the eigenvector nearest the castle topic changes rank and turns through about 51°, and every eigenvector mixes signs | Appendix H of Part III of the owner's LEGO monograph builds two co-occurrence matrices from nonnegative topics. One has topics for spaceship and castle; the other splits spaceship into wings and engines and keeps castle unchanged. The monograph reads castle's survival as a stable eigenmode and calls that archetype persistence. Computed here: the topics overlap (ship·castle = 0.21), so no eigenvector is the castle topic. The eigenvector closest to it is the second mode at rank 2 (cosine 0.873) and the first at rank 3 (0.926), about 51° apart. Persistence of a generating factor does not show as persistence of an eigenvector, which is what [CLAIM-148](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-148.md)'s identifiability limits predict. | Active |
| [CASE-098](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-098.md) | A long rivalry between two teams outlives every player, owner and supporter who first carried it: new fans inherit the antagonism, its history and its practices before they know why the game matters | From U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16 on sports fandom (the owner's list of subcases). A2's reading: a mature rivalry is "a reproduced intercollective relation", carried by families, media and fan culture, that can survive the replacement of everyone on both sides. Stipulated: the record has no study of a particular rivalry. It shows a relation with its own continuity; it does not show that the relation is a system, an agent, or constitutive of either fandom. | Active |
| [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md) | The two-hypothesis coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state: a meaning bias m and an authority bias a, each stable alone, coupled by authority shaping interpretation (β) and interpretation shaping endorsement (γ) | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. Near the symmetric state of the two-hypothesis, two-specialist model, (m, a) evolves by a 2×2 matrix J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] plus noise. With nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the symmetric state is unstable exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ), and the unstable direction mixes meaning and authority. Checked here. A construction about a linearization, not a fitted or simulated result. | Active |
| [CASE-100](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-100.md) | A fan redub of an X-Men cartoon, circulated online in 2006, put "I'm the Juggernaut, bitch!" into X-Men: The Last Stand three months later | The owner's case at U7 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, offered as a fandom "making something happen". Two fans made the parody; many people spread it for their own reasons; the film's makers put its line in at a reshoot. A7: an effect on an outside institution with no collective intention and no procedure behind it. Documented as to the sequence; the route by which the parody reached the decision, and whether the spreaders were X-Men fans or the internet at large, is not. | Active |
| [CASE-101](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md) | Three simulated populations with the same turnover and the same aggregate statistics: one whose members respond alike to a common input, one that transmits its norms to its replacements, and one held together by an institution that selects and trains its members | Proposed three times in the exchange of 2026-10-16 (A11 §9, A12 §7 and A13 §5), as the place where criteria of individuality should disagree: Krakauer et al.'s temporal measures, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, Hoel's effective information and the block criterion of [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md). The common-input arm is Bourrat's "reconstructed entity" ([LIT-005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md)), which the record already holds and the exchange did not cite. Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-102](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-102.md) | A college program stays good, or bad, at a sport for decades while its whole roster turns over every four or five years | The owner's case, U3 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "the team composition experiences extremely fast churn, and yet in spite of this real world ship-of-theseus situation, teams often maintain standing on similar timescales as professional teams (if not longer)". A3: it separates the persistence of a collective's identity from the persistence of its capacities, and the second needs a mechanism that regenerates them in each new population. Stipulated: the record holds no data on program persistence. The proposed test is residual persistence of performance across seasons with no player overlap. | Active |
| [CASE-103](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-103.md) | A fanbase keeps a reputation, for hostility or loyalty or knowledge, after the behaviour that earned it has changed, and outsiders and members both act on it | From U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A2 separated three things that vary independently: many members have the trait; others believe the fanbase has it; that belief shapes how the fanbase behaves. A reputation belongs to a fanbase through its relations with audiences, and it can enter the process that produces its own evidence. It is a case for regulative attribution ([THEORY-137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-137.md), [QUESTION-049](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-049.md)) beyond mental states. Stipulated; it shows no particular reputation was self-fulfilling. | Active |
| [CASE-104](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-104.md) | A fanbase is said to hate its owner or general manager, though it has no procedure for forming a view, some fans approve of the person, and nobody has counted | From U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A2 separated four things the sentence could report: a statistical aggregate of dislike, a shared emotional orientation, a norm of opposition that a loyal fan is expected to meet, and a corporate judgment such as a supporters' trust demanding resignation. A fanbase can have the second and third without the fourth, and a vocal minority can set a public stance most members privately reject. The case for [QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md). Stipulated. | Active |
| [CASE-105](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-105.md) | The Washington Senators: the original club became the Minnesota Twins in 1961, an expansion club took its name in Washington and became the Texas Rangers in 1972, and the Montreal Expos became the Washington Nationals in 2005, so franchise, city and supporters each have a different successor | The owner's subcase at U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, "the team formerly known as the washington senators". A2 corrected the framing: the name belonged to two franchises, and the city's present team descends from a third. A league can designate the successor franchise; it cannot designate the successor fandom. The lineages are documented; how supporters actually distributed their loyalties is not, and the case does not show that a fandom's identity branched. | Active |
| [CASE-106](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md) | The two-hypothesis linearization with endorsement scored on committed predictions: when the shared meaning bends the specialists' predictions with weight κ and the reading of the evidence with weight κ′, the coupling of interpretation to endorsement is γ = 4ηs(κ′ − κ̄) | Built for [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md)'s formal question: is scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? The construction keeps [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s two-hypothesis linearization and replaces the score with squared error between each specialist's committed prediction and the evidence as read. The coupling γ then has the sign of κ′ − κ̄: corrective when the interpretation bends the predictions more than the reading of the evidence, null when equally, capturing when less. Checked symbolically, and the stability conditions against 200,000 random draws. Fictional by construction. | Active |
| [CASE-107](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-107.md) | Locked-in syndrome: consciousness preserved with anarthria and quadriplegia; in the classic form, vertical eye movement and blinking remain and carry communication, and in the completely locked-in state no motor channel remains | The owner's case, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "a lucid human who struggles with locked-in syndrome". It separates lucid judgement from limb and speech action. In the classic form it does not separate judgement from action as active inference defines it, since the eye movements it spares are that theory's model action. The completely locked-in state is the real test, and there any evidence of lucidity has to come through a channel that is itself an action. Visceromotor regulation and Damasio's internal "as if body loop" survive paralysis, so the case never removes every contingency between intention and outcome. | Active |
| [CASE-108](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-108.md) | Robust governance under internal compromise: four governance architectures over cooperative, honestly dissenting and adversarial specialists, scored on attack success and on what the safeguards cost, with a variant that compromises the evaluators | A41's proposed study, from the exchange of 2026-10-17, on the owner's U41 question about insider threats. A multitask learner with three kinds of specialist (cooperative, honest but dissenting, adversarial) is run under unrestricted, reliability-weighted, role-limited and adaptive governance, and scored on lost legitimate capability, suppressed honest minorities, cost of safeguards and repair of governance after failure, as well as on attack success. Its sharpest variant compromises the processes that evaluate the others' competence, which tests [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md)'s independent scoring. Federated learning is the natural testbed. Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-109](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-109.md) | Two people with the same demanding commitment, the same output and the same effort in the work, who differ in how their intrapersonal conflict is settled: one escalates it to deliberate override, the other's processes accommodate one another | The owner's case, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, worked by A45 as Person A ("repeated escalation") and Person B ("local coordination") on one writing project. Both exert real effort and produce work of equal quality; only the route by which conflict is settled differs. It is the variation [CASE-013](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-013.md) and [CASE-051](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-051.md) lack: there one writer's effort varies across afternoons, here effort in the work is held high in both. It is used for [CLAIM-358](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-358.md). Stipulated, so it shows what the claim distinguishes, not that people differ this way. | Active |
| [CASE-110](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md) | Two members, one total: a coarse-graining by total output preserves an institution's performance, its survival and every prediction it makes, and still merges a state in which a member works within the agreed cap with one in which that member works far past it | A22's Construction C of the exchange of 2026-10-17, "Institutional performance versus constituent capability", which A22 proposed and did not write out, from A21 §5 and §16; written out here in its smallest form. Two members share twelve hours of work. Total output decides the institution's performance and its survival, so the total is sufficient for every institutional judgment, and the policies (6, 6) and (10, 2) have the same total. A member's claim not to work past an agreed cap of eight hours tells them apart, so by [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md) no judgment on the total recovers it. Fictional by construction; it shows a possibility, not how often institutions are like this. | Active |
| [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) | A fold in boundary maintenance: in ḃ = μb + κb² − b³ with cooperative repair (κ > 0), an unmaintained and a maintained state are both stable for −κ²/4 < μ < 0, so maintenance lost past the fold is not restored by returning the parameter, and recovery slows to zero as the fold nears | A7 §4 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, after the owner's "flesh this out further": a normal form for the activity b that maintains a boundary, in which repair processes reinforce one another. Its equilibria, the bistable range, the hysteresis loop and the slowing of recovery at the fold are derived and rechecked here. It shows a capacity to maintain, and not only a state, being lost and not coming back when conditions do, which is [CLAIM-099](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-099.md)'s distinction in a model. The experts agreed Warhol's silkscreen changed the photograph's meaning, from Prince's private identity to his public image. The majority held that this did not matter for the use at issue: a magazine cover illustrating a story about Prince serves substantially the photograph's own purpose, and new meaning counts only as evidence of a different purpose.
